references.text: The Amalekites are first mentioned as Israel's enemy in the wilderness, when they attacked Israel at Rephidim.
Amalek was a descendant of Esau and lived in the Negev region.
The Hittites, Amorites, and Canaanites are mentioned among the peoples living in the Promised Land in God's covenant with Abram.
The same nations (Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Jebusites) are mentioned as inhabitants of the land God would give to Israel.
Moses recounts the mountainous regions of the Amorites and the coastal lands of the Canaanites, the same geographical distribution found in Num 13:29.
The Amorites in the mountains and the Canaanites by the sea are described in the same way when Israel crossed the Jordan.
Joshua describes the Canaanites in the east and west, and the Amorites, Hittites, and Jebusites in the mountains—the same geographical pattern.
The Jebusites and Amorites are mentioned among the original peoples of Canaan.
The Jebusites lived in Jerusalem, which was located in the mountainous region, confirming their placement in Num 13:29.
The kingdom of the Amorites under Sihon confirms their presence in the mountainous regions east of the Jordan.
